title: Are Machine Rationales (Not) Useful to Humans? Measuring and Improving Human Utility of Free-text Rationales
why: Measures and improves the human utility of free-text machine-generated rationales; a rationale-quality evaluation paper, not a stopping-rule regret study.

title: Accelerating Transformer Inference for Translation via Parallel Decoding
why: Proposes parallel (Jacobi-style) decoding to accelerate transformer translation inference; a decoding-speed method for machine translation, not an online stopping-rule regret study.

title: Are Human Explanations Always Helpful? Towards Objective Evaluation of Human Natural Language Explanations
why: Asks whether human natural-language explanations are always helpful and proposes an objective evaluation metric; an explanation-evaluation paper, unrelated to reasoning-stopping regret.

title: ArgU: A Controllable Factual Argument Generator
why: ArgU is a controllable factual argument generator conditioned on stance and scheme; an argument-generation method paper, not a stopping-rule regret study.

title: Aggregating Multiple Heuristic Signals as Supervision for Unsupervised Automated Essay Scoring
why: ULRA aggregates heuristic signals as supervision for unsupervised automated essay scoring; an essay-scoring method paper, unrelated to reasoning-stopping regret.

title: A Universal Discriminator for Zero-Shot Generalization
why: Introduces a universal discriminator unifying discriminative NLP tasks under one true/false formulation for zero-shot generalization; a task-unification method paper, not a stopping-rule regret study.

title: ALERT: Adapt Language Models to Reasoning Tasks
why: ALERT adapts language models to reasoning tasks via typed prompting; a reasoning-adaptation method paper, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: ArgAnalysis35K : A large-scale dataset for Argument Quality Analysis
why: ArgAnalysis35K is a large-scale dataset for argument-quality analysis; a dataset-construction paper, not a stopping-rule regret study.

title: An Empirical Analysis of Parameter-Efficient Methods for Debiasing Pre-Trained Language Models
why: Empirically compares parameter-efficient tuning methods (prefix/prompt/adapter) for debiasing PLMs; a debiasing-method comparison, unrelated to reasoning-stopping regret.

title: A Cautious Generalization Goes a Long Way: Learning Morphophonological Rules
why: Learns morphophonological rules via cautious generalization; a linguistic rule-learning paper, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: AlignScore: Evaluating Factual Consistency with A Unified Alignment Function
why: AlignScore is a unified alignment function for evaluating factual consistency; a factual-consistency evaluation-metric paper, not a stopping-rule regret study.

title: APOLLO: A Simple Approach for Adaptive Pretraining of Language Models for Logical Reasoning
why: APOLLO adapts pretraining objectives for logical reasoning via sentence-level entailment classification; a pretraining-adaptation method paper, unrelated to reasoning-stopping regret.

title: Being Right for Whose Right Reasons?
why: Studies whose 'right reasons' models are being right for in rationale-based explanation methods; an explanation-faithfulness study, not a stopping-rule regret study.

title: A Survey on Zero Pronoun Translation
why: Surveys zero-pronoun translation methods; a machine-translation survey, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: Binary and Ternary Natural Language Generation
why: Studies ternary/binary weight-and-activation quantization for generative transformers; a model-compression paper, unrelated to reasoning-stopping regret.

title: An Extensible Plug-and-Play Method for Multi-Aspect Controllable Text Generation
why: Proposes an extensible plug-and-play method for multi-aspect controllable text generation; a controllable-generation architecture paper, not a stopping-rule regret study.

title: A Crosslingual Investigation of Conceptualization in 1335 Languages
why: Investigates conceptualization patterns across 1335 languages; a crosslingual semantics paper, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: A Measure-Theoretic Characterization of Tight Language Models
why: Gives a measure-theoretic characterization of when language models are 'tight' (no probability mass leak); a formal language-model-theory paper, unrelated to reasoning-stopping regret.

title: BITE: Textual Backdoor Attacks with Iterative Trigger Injection
why: BITE is an iterative-trigger-injection textual backdoor attack; a security/backdoor-attack paper, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: Adaptive and Personalized Exercise Generation for Online Language Learning
why: Generates adaptive, personalized exercises for online language learning via constrained beam search; an education-application paper, unrelated to reasoning-stopping regret.

title: Attributable and Scalable Opinion Summarization
why: Proposes an unsupervised hierarchical discrete-latent-space method for attributable opinion summarization; a summarization-method paper, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: Better Simultaneous Translation with Monotonic Knowledge Distillation
why: Uses two-stage monotonic knowledge distillation to improve simultaneous machine translation; a simultaneous-translation training method, not a stopping-rule regret study (its read/write policy is a fixed monotonic training target, not an online oracle-regret measurement).

title: Best-k Search Algorithm for Neural Text Generation
why: Best-k search is a deterministic decoding algorithm balancing quality and diversity in neural text generation; a decoding-algorithm paper for generation quality, not an online stopping-rule regret study.

title: Automatic Annotation of Direct Speech in Written French Narratives
why: Builds the largest annotated French direct-speech corpus and benchmarks sequence-labeling models; a dataset/benchmark paper for narrative analysis, unrelated to reasoning-stopping regret.

title: Analyzing Transformers in Embedding Space
why: Analyzes transformer sublayer updates directly in vocabulary embedding space; a mechanistic-interpretability method, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: Attention as a Guide for Simultaneous Speech Translation
why: EDATT is an attention-guided adaptive read/write policy for simultaneous speech translation; a genuinely adjacent 'online adaptive decision from an internal signal' mechanism, but for a different task (streaming translation read/write) and without any oracle-regret construction, so it is rejected rather than selected as adjacent.

title: A Comparative Study on the Impact of Model Compression Techniques on Fairness in Language Models
why: Compares pruning/distillation/quantization compression techniques for their effect on LM fairness; a model-compression fairness study, unrelated to reasoning-stopping regret.

title: Abductive Commonsense Reasoning Exploiting Mutually Exclusive Explanations
why: LiPoR performs abductive commonsense reasoning by exploiting mutually exclusive explanations; a commonsense-reasoning method paper, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: An AMR-based Link Prediction Approach for Document-level Event Argument Extraction

title: Beyond Contrastive Learning: A Variational Generative Model for Multilingual Retrieval
why: Proposes a variational generative model for multilingual retrieval beyond contrastive learning; a retrieval-representation-learning paper, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: Bidirectional Generative Framework for Cross-domain Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis
why: Proposes a bidirectional generative framework for cross-domain aspect-based sentiment analysis; a sentiment-analysis method paper, unrelated to test-time reasoning-stopping regret.

title: SAFER: Risk-Constrained Sample-then-Filter in Large Language Models

title: The First Impression Problem: Internal Bias Triggers Overthinking in Reasoning Models
